steps.text: Mix cottage cheese, flour, eggs, and oil together in a large bowl.

Spray a large skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium heat. Pour 1/3 cup batter for each pancake onto the skillet. Cook until bubbles appear on the surface, 3 to 5 minutes. Flip and cook until browned on the other side, 3 to 4 minutes more. Serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Cottage Cheese Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: These cottage cheese pancakes are tender, fluffy, and easy to make with just five ingredients for a tasty and filling way to the day!

review.reviewBody: This recipe actually turned out really good. It does sound odd but it tasted really good with a few changes: 1) I used my food processor for the cottage cheese because I prefer without the lumps. 2) I added 1/2 teaspoon of vanilla extract. 3) Used whole wheat flour instead of white. 4) I also added 1/2 tsp of baking powder. I didn't use any sugar because with the maple syrup was enought for my taste. It's a great breakfast with a great source of protein and no fat, if you use fat free cottage cheese. Thanks for the recipe Jennifer, I will definitely make it again!

Excellent recipe. My own take: No need to blend the cottage cheese - as it melts from the heat it becomes creamy. Very important - do not change the flour content - it's important to have enough starch to bind the cottage cheese. Also - high/full fat cottage cheese is better - make sure it's not watery! Lastly, I use avocado oil, because you should make sure the pan is very hot! I had about a tablespoon or two of oil in a non stick pan! This is important as if the pan is not hot enough, or it's not a non stick pan it will stick! Make sure you wait a few minutes for it to cook before flipping! I sprinkle some wild organic blueberries on one side before flipping and for serving some PURE maple syrup. ENJOY!

Loved these! I did add some cinnamon, which was nice. I spread them with fig jam. Would also be great with honey. Next time I'm going to add a pinch of salt, though. UPDATE: I make these for my family all the time and my kids love them. I love that they have extra protein and nutrition for their growing bodies! I always throw together all of the ingredients and blend them with an immersion blender. You can't even tell there's cottage cheese that way. I do add a pinch of salt, cinnamon, and some vanilla typically. I really like adding raisins, but my kids prefer without. A lifelong keeper!

Truly delicious and quick and easy to prepare . My only suggestion would be to use a high-speed blender, like a ninja to combine the eggs and the cottage cheese. I would also substitute one of the eggs with a quarter cup of whatever milk is preferred.

With tweaks i made i'd give it 5 stars. this is an excellent protein-packed pancake and my kids loved them too drizzled with some maple syurp so it's a huge win!!

i made the following tweaks:
- instead of plain flour i used rolled oats and used 1/2 cup
- i omitted the oil
- used 4 eggs
- added pinch of salt, 1 tsp vanilla, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp honey

i blend everything in my blender and let the batter sit for 10 mins. i find this helped the pancakes cook thicker.

This recipe was very good, but lacked Baking Powder which was in others recipes I researched. The addition of 1/2 TBSP of baking powder produced a fluffier pancake. I also experimented with other flours besides all-purpose flour and all were equally as good, including gluten and grain-free varieties. Add the baking powder and this is a 5-star recipe. I also have added fruit including blueberries and apples, which all produced a great result.

I've been making this for decades. I used to always make it when our kids were little and we had a long day outing ahead - the high protein content really satisfied them so that they didn't get hungry again for hours! 
I do have a few changes:
1. Put ingredients in the blender and the pour into pan. It tastes better when the batter is smooth plus its easier this way!
2. Halve the oil. I only use 1 Tablespoon per recipe (I usually double the recipe so 2 T oil total).
3. I'm gluten intolerant now so I've adapted the recipe replacing the flour with Pamela's baking & pancake mix (same amount as called for in recipe). Still tastes great.
Also, unlike regular pancakes, these are delicious reheated the next day! I also tried saving the batter to make again but it turns out better and is simpler to just make all the pancakes at one and then store the leftovers in the fridge for the next day (or two).
My favorite topping is with applesauce & a little maple syrup. My husband prefers with strawberries & Cool Whip.

These pancakes are AMAZING - I'm suprised they don't have more reviews. They are not your typical dry pancakes, they are moist and full of protein. I prefer to use "oat flour" instead of regular flour (to make oat flour: put 1-cup of quick oats into your blender for a minute until there are no oat chunks left). I also puree my cottage cheese in the blender so the pancake batter is smooth, not chunky. I usually make a triple-batch of these because they keep well in the fridge for a couple days for quick weekday morning breakfasts. You can either make them all into pancakes and keep them in the fridge cooked, OR you can just make the batter and store it that way. For a triple batch: puree 3-cups of quick oats, 1 (750ml) container of cottage cheese (add milk as necessary to blend, approx 1/3-cup), 10-12 eggs, and some canola oil. You could also toss in some whey protein powder for added protein. They are delish served with either maple syrup or homemade fruit syrup. **Update** I made a triple batch of this pancake batter before our family camping trip and took it along with us. I cooked them up each morning on a cookie sheet over a propane grill (on low), and they were fantastic!! They cooked fast (soon as they dry up around edges, they need to be flipped - approx 1-min each side). These will definitely be a staple camping recipe now!

These were amazing! I added a scoop of vanilla protein powder and a 1/2 Tbls of baking powder. I also pureed the cottage cheese because I really wanted to not even know I'm eating it (I don't like cottage cheese) because I wanted more protein in my breakfast!

Made these and loved them. Used Carb Balance instead of flour simply to limit carbs and added a scoop of whey protein because, well, protein! But geez these were good. I used a blender to combine all ingredients, put berries on top. Wife hates the idea of blended cottage cheese - NEVER KNEW - I admitted later - she was shocked how much she enjoyed these pancakes. Will definitely make again.
Added the zest of one lemon, half tsp each of vanilla and baking powder. Served with sliced frozen strawberries heated in the microwave.
Love this
Very simple and even my picky, carb-loving kid enjoyed it.
Takes long too cook but oh so worth it!
Good for adults. Kids didn't really like.
Super easy to make. I made a double batch and added a teaspoon of vanilla extract to add more depth of flavor. The result was yummy. For my next batch, I might experiment with almond extract :-)

I was pleasantly surprised by this recipe. I didn’t read the comments in advance, but also used my ninja to blend the ingredients. I added a splash of vanilla extract. These have a more crepe like texture than a typical pancake, but they were still great. I will definitely try oat or whole wheat flour next time and also considered a bit of baking powder, but the recipe is good as is and one of the better protein pancakes I’ve tried.

I liked it and so did family. I doubled the recipe for family of 5 which includes 3 adults and 2 teens, and it was just about perfect amount. I used 1/2 whole wheat and 1/2 white flour, added a banana for a bit of sweetness without processed sugar, about a teaspoon of almond extract, sprinkled cinnamon, about a teaspoon of baking powder. I also blended the cottage cheese so there were no lumps. They are flatter than regular pancakes and have a bit of an eggy taste, which is fine for those who like it. We served with blueberries, maple syrup, pecans, and whipped cream and it made a very nice base. I may experiment with apples vs bananas, maybe different types of flour (ground oats, or maybe almond flour). I may also try a lower fat cottage cheese (used full 4% fat cottage cheese) and some ground walnuts or pecans. Good basic higher protein recipe which I appreciate with 2 vegetarians in the house.
For a double recipe I added 1T vanilla, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp baking pwdr, 3 Tbls sugar, 2-3 Tbls flour. My picky eater that needs protein loved them.
They are like a Dutch pancake. I blended the batter on my Vitamix and added some cinnamon and sugar. A little vanilla will help with added flavor.
